head: Iron sharpens iron
paras: The Capitals have won three straight, while the Wild (9-3-3) lost 4-3 in overtime to the Islanders on Thursday. Going in, the Wild are first in the Central (second in the NHL) and the Capitals second in the Metropolitan (tied for tenth).
The Wild’s record (.700) is about what their chances are worth. The Capitals’ record (.667) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.575), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Wild leave the shooting to their forwards (3rd lowest), let the point shots come and guard the net (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). Minnesota has allowed 2.33 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. On the other side, the Capitals have had some of the league’s best goaltending (3rd) and get their shots through to the net (5th). They also get the league’s best looks (1st), so their good looks will be harder to come by against the Wild. The Wild’s power play (10th) could do real damage against the Caps’ penalty kill (27th).

Kirill Kaprizov (14 G / 10 A / 24 P in 15 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is tied for second in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Quinn Hughes (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 15 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Washington. Alex Tuch (10 G / 2 A / 12 P in 12 GP) is tied for the Capitals’ scoring lead. Dylan Strome (3 G / 9 A / 12 P in 12 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games.
Jesper Wallstedt (8-2-3 / .916 SV% in 13 GS) has been terrific for Minnesota and will likely start. Logan Thompson (5-3-0 / .903 SV% in 8 GS) is in line to start for Washington.
At home, Spencer Carbery likes to send Protas, Dubois and Wilson out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy.

items.text: Kirill Kaprizov is one point from 500.

The Wild are newly without Jared Spurgeon, have been without Marcus Foligno since Oct 8, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Jesper Wallstedt is expected to start.
The Capitals have been without Rasmus Sandin for several games.
Jordan Kyrou has eight goals in eleven games against Minnesota since 2023-24, most of them with St. Louis.

WSH.head: A slightly uphill night for the Capitals
WSH.body: Even though Washington has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Capitals can tip it if they get good looks.

MIN.head: The Wild start a half-step ahead
MIN.body: Even though Washington has home-ice advantage, Minnesota has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Capitals can still swing it if they get good looks.

calls.head: Iron sharpens iron
calls.body: The Capitals are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Wild are near the top at preventing dangerous shots. Hot take: the Capitals break through anyway.

calls.head: Top line on top line: Wilson vs. Kaprizov
calls.body: At home, the Capitals keep sending Wilson’s line (Protas, Dubois and Wilson) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Spencer Carbery has been choosing strength on strength. Tonight the Wild’s first line is Kaprizov, Ek and Boldy.

calls.head: Penalties could cost the Capitals
calls.body: The Capitals’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Wild’s power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Capitals tonight.

calls.head: A long night for Logan Thompson
calls.body: The Wild shoot a lot, and the Capitals are near the bottom of the league at keeping shots down. Look for a big shot total.
